standard.coverage: Remainder of New York State -- everywhere OUTSIDE New York City, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester. Recorded as the standard because it is the lower of the two and applies to the larger land area; the downstate rate is in variants and must be used for those four jurisdictions.
standard.note: N.Y. Lab. Law 652 as amended in 2023: $16.00 upstate / $17.00 downstate for 2026, then CPI indexing from 2027.

tipped.note: Upstate FOOD SERVICE worker cash wage. New York splits tipped employees into food service workers and 'service employees' with different credits, and does so separately in each region -- four tipped figures in total, all in variants.

variants.label: New York City, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester counties
variants.test: Work performed in NYC or in Nassau, Suffolk or Westchester county.
variants.note: A payroll engine keyed on a bare two-letter state code cannot get New York right; this is a genuine county-level split inside a state file.

variants.label: Service employee cash wage (remainder of state)

sources.title: New York State Department of Labor -- Minimum Wage (rates effective 01/01/2026)
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. Source of all six New York figures: $17.00 downstate / $16.00 remainder, food service worker cash wages of $11.35 / $10.70 (tip credits $5.65 / $5.30), and service employee cash wages of $14.15 / $13.30 (tip credits $2.85 / $2.70).

sources.title: U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division -- State Minimum Wage Laws (table current as of July 1, 2026)
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. DOL's own state-by-state table is the spine of every standard rate in this database; where a state's own labor department was ALSO read directly, that source is listed too and wins on any disagreement (see South Dakota's tipped cash wage for the one case where they disagreed).

sources.title: U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division -- Minimum Wages for Tipped Employees (table current as of July 1, 2026)
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. Source of the combined rate / maximum tip credit / minimum cash wage triple and the 'tipped employee' monthly-tips definition for every state and territory in this database.

knownGaps: New York's HOME CARE AIDE minimum wage is a separate, higher figure set by Public Health Law 3614-f; NYSDOL publishes it in fact sheet P105, which was not read this pass. No figure is asserted here rather than guessed.
The hospitality and building-service wage orders carry their own allowances (uniform maintenance, meals, lodging) that can change the effective cash figure; not modelled.

This engine's own garnishment data (data/garnishment/state-overrides-2026.json) uses the LOWER $16.00 figure for New York's 30x minimum-wage floor and discloses that as a simplification. Both files are now consistent about the fact that there are two rates.
